public_rationale: Only the training-increase forecast is scored. The accessible annual figures show higher R&D compute spending, including $8.3 billion in 2025, but do not clearly reconcile that category with the $3 billion training baseline. The original report that may establish the comparison could not be read. These gaps prevent a decisive finding; they are not evidence that training costs failed to rise.
limitations: The distinction between training and broader research spending materially affects the comparison.
Experimental training counts; this assessment does not restrict training to final runs.
The qualified $6 billion server-cost counterfactual is not scored.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's training costs, currently $3 billion a year, will almost certainly increase; without Microsoft's discount its server costs would likely be about $6 billion a year.

statement.excerpt: This means that OpenAI would likely be burning more like $6 billion a year on server costs if it wasn’t so deeply wedded to Microsoft — and that's before you get into costs like staffing ($1.5 billion a year), and, as I've discussed, training costs that are currently $3 billion for the year and will almost certainly increase.

our_interpretation: Score only the training-cost increase forecast. The qualified server-cost counterfactual is outside the scored commitment.
The baseline is the cited $3 billion annual training-cost estimate for 2024.
An increase means a subsequent calendar year's aggregate training costs exceed that baseline on a comparable basis.
Training includes experimental and unsuccessful training work; it is not restricted to final runs for released models.
No deadline is supplied. A later spending projection alone does not establish that the increase happened.
A broader R&D total requires a reconciliation to the baseline training category before it can settle the forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable reporting establishes that OpenAI incurred more than $3 billion in comparable annual training costs in a calendar year after 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A definitive end to OpenAI's model-training activity, with a complete comparable spending record, establishes that no subsequent annual training total exceeded $3 billion. A temporary decline or lack of an increase so far is insufficient.
